title: Exception hierarchy and exit codes in exceptions.py
answers: Which exceptions have exit code 2 vs 1?
body:
exceptions.py:
- ClickException(Exception): class attr exit_code=1; __init__ caches show_color via resolve_color_default() (ctx gone by print time); format_message() returns message; show() prints 'Error: msg' to stderr.
- UsageError(ClickException): exit_code=2, holds ctx; show() prints usage from ctx.get_usage(), 'Try ... --help' hint if help option exists, then Error line; uses ctx.color. Subclasses: BadParameter (→MissingParameter), NoSuchOption, NoSuchCommand, BadOptionUsage, BadArgumentUsage, NoArgsIsHelpError (show prints help text via echo).
- FileError(ClickException): stays exit_code 1.
- Abort and Exit subclass RuntimeError, NOT ClickException; Exit has __slots__ exit_code (default 0).
- core.py Context.fail→raise UsageError(msg, self); Context.abort→Abort; Context.exit(code) calls self.close() then raises Exit.
